      "explanation": "The compact dismissal answers the alleged problem of excessive empathy without explaining why empathy cannot be excessive in the relevant circumstances.     },

      "startEvent": 963,
      "endEvent": 970,
      "contextStartEvent": 944,
      "contextEndEvent": 1009,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "Institutional religion is always failing. And then it's always recovering, right?",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["comfort", "identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Responding to institutional decline, Douthat incorporates both failure and recovery into a scripturally promised pattern, insulating religious confidence against either trajectory (E969–1009). Biblical examples supply reasons for expecting failures, but whether they earn the unrestricted recovery claim is unclear. He nevertheless acknowledges actual institutional wrongdoing at E953–962 rather than denying it."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1273,
      "endEvent": 1278,
      "contextStartEvent": 1247,
      "contextEndEvent": 1284,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "I don't think there's any version of AI that would disprove the existence of God.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",

      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "AI advances confirm his worldview at E1263–1275, while no AI version could disprove God at E1276–1278. This suggests asymmetric treatment, but the question concerns a bounded technological development whose disconfirming relevance is not established. He offers an ordinary design inference, not a catchphrase; his separate resurrection concession at E1224–1230 limits broader immunity claims."
    }
